title: Introduce probing contracts and compact change-lens for lightweight release previews
author: Elena Ruiz
description:
Motivation: model onboarding currently produces large, noisy release notes and model profiles when telemetry is sparse. This PR adds two complementary pieces: (1) a probing contract abstraction (lightweight declarative probes that run small deterministic workloads against incoming model artifacts) and (2) a compact change-lens that synthesizes a short, human-friendly release preview (<=3 bullets) from the combined onboarding metadata and probe results. The goal is to give reviewers a high-signal preview of changes (compatibility, perf delta, token footprint) without waiting for full population of profile telemetry.

What this PR does (high level):
- Add a "probing contract" DSL and runner to models/onboard. Contracts are small YAML manifests that declare probes (prompt template, input shard, expected stability buckets) and lightweight validators (latency_threshold_ms, mem_delta_pct, semantic_consistency_check). Contracts are scoped per-source and attach to onboard artifacts during intake.
- Implement an in-repo probes runner (registry/probes/runner.py) that executes contracts inside a sandboxed, rate-limited worker and emits structured probe records (jsonl) and a concise probe-summary blob used by downstream tooling.
- Introduce change-lens synthesizer (changelog/lens.py) that consumes model metadata, declared contracts, and probe summaries to generate a compact release preview: three prioritized bullets (compatibility risks, perf delta, recommended tags/rollout plan). The change-lens is intentionally conservative (prefers false negatives) and surfaces a confidence score.
- Wire the synthesizer into the onboarding pipeline: onboard hooks now emit a preview draft as part of the pre-approve artifact (console + Linear comment).
- Add unit and integration tests, plus sample contract manifests and a small e2e harness for CI.

Notes on design decisions: the probing contract DSL is intentionally minimal to encourage adoption by solutions engineers; contracts are ephemeral and do not replace full performance profiles or long-running benchmarks. The change-lens uses a lightweight heuristic ranker (feature-weighted rules) rather than a learned model to remain auditable in the release flow.

Checklist: 
- [x] Probing contract DSL + schema + loader
- [x] Probes runner with sandbox/timeouts
- [x] Probe summary serializer (compact jsonl)
- [x] Change-lens synthesizer + prioritization rules
- [x] Integrations: onboarding hook + console preview endpoint
- [x] Tests: unit + integration + a small e2e CI job
- [x] Docs: short how-to + examples in docs/onboard/quickstart.md

Related: swaps ideas from ENG-743 and earlier work on digesters but purposefully differs by focusing on an early-stage preview (not a replacement for full changelogs). See Linear ENG-9621 for adoption plan and rollout gating.

Security/Cost: runner executes small synthetic workloads; we added a per-tenant budget guard and global rate limiter to avoid noisy intake storms. All probe artifacts respect PII rules and default to redacting model-provided prompts unless explicitly allowed by the onboard manifest.

release_notes:
- Add lightweight probing contracts to capture early compatibility and perf signals during model intake.
- Introduce compact change-lens that synthesizes a 3-line release preview for faster human review.
- Add sandboxed probes runner with rate limiting and redaction guards.

Impact: low-risk feature behind opt-in; defaults are conservative. Admins can enable probes per-tenant. Rollout plan: staged opt-in for dev/test tenants, then gradual enablement for solutions-engineered onboards (see ENG-9621).
notes_for_changelog_reviewers: The preview is not authoritative; reviewers should still rely on full profile artifacts when available. If reviewers prefer not to see previews, set the onboarding flow flag PREVIEW_DRAFT=false. The contract DSL is intentionally small; teams wanting richer probes should extend the DSL and add guarded runners.
